tools.name: Qiskit
tools.summary: Build quantum circuits, work with quantum information, and transpile programs for a target device.
tools.bestFor: Learning gate-based computing and developing circuits for the IBM Quantum ecosystem.
tools.execution: Local state tools; simulators and IBM hardware through companion packages.
tools.access: Open-source SDK. IBM cloud execution requires an account and an eligible access plan.
tools.limit: The SDK alone does not provide cloud hardware access. Large state simulations need substantial classical memory.

tools.name: Cirq
tools.summary: Create, transform, and simulate circuits with device constraints and noise in mind.
tools.bestFor: Circuit experiments, parameter sweeps, and ideal or noisy simulation.
tools.execution: Local state-vector and density-matrix simulation; provider integrations for devices.
tools.access: Open-source library. Access to a physical device depends on its provider.
tools.limit: Installing Cirq does not grant access to Google quantum hardware. General simulation grows costly with qubit count.

tools.name: PennyLane
tools.summary: Connect trainable quantum circuits to automatic differentiation and classical machine-learning libraries.
tools.bestFor: Variational algorithms, quantum chemistry, and experiments with hybrid quantum machine learning.
tools.execution: Local simulators and compatible hardware plugins.
tools.access: Open-source framework. Hardware plugins have their own provider requirements.
tools.limit: Trainability, encoding cost, and measurement noise matter. A hybrid model does not imply a quantum advantage.

tools.name: Microsoft QDK
tools.summary: Develop quantum programs with Q#, simulation, debugging, and resource-estimation workflows.
tools.bestFor: Structured algorithm development and exploring the resources a future quantum program could need.
tools.execution: Local development and simulation; Azure Quantum provider jobs through a workspace.
tools.access: Free, open-source development kit. Cloud execution needs an Azure Quantum workspace and provider access.
tools.limit: Resource estimates depend on assumptions about algorithms, error rates, and hardware; they are not runtime measurements.

tools.name: Amazon Braket SDK
tools.summary: Define quantum tasks with a common Python interface for local simulation and Amazon Braket devices.
tools.bestFor: Moving a small circuit from local testing to supported cloud simulators or hardware.
tools.execution: Local simulator; managed simulators and supported QPUs on AWS.
tools.access: Open-source SDK. Local simulation needs no AWS account; cloud tasks require AWS access and may incur charges.
tools.limit: Available operations and device capabilities differ. Review device requirements and cloud pricing before submitting tasks.

tools.name: CUDA-Q
tools.summary: Write quantum kernels in a programming model that connects classical computing, simulation, and QPU targets.
tools.bestFor: Hybrid quantum-classical workflows and CPU or GPU circuit-simulation experiments.
tools.execution: CPU and supported GPU simulators; supported hardware backends.
tools.access: Open-source platform. GPU use needs compatible hardware and software; QPU access follows provider terms.
tools.limit: GPU acceleration depends on the target and platform. It accelerates classical simulation, rather than turning a GPU into a QPU.

tools.name: cuQuantum
tools.summary: GPU libraries for state-vector and tensor-network calculations used in quantum-computing simulation.
tools.bestFor: Accelerating compatible classical simulators and tensor-network workloads on NVIDIA GPUs.
tools.execution: Classical GPU computation, including supported multi-GPU workflows.
tools.access: NVIDIA software with package-specific license terms and CUDA compatibility requirements.
tools.limit: This is a simulation library stack, not a cloud quantum computer. Memory, tensor structure, and GPU compatibility constrain workloads.

tools.name: TKET / pytket
tools.summary: Build, optimize, place, and route quantum circuits for different target backends.
tools.bestFor: Studying circuit compilation and adapting a program to a device’s native gates and connectivity.
tools.execution: Circuit compilation; simulator and hardware extensions.
tools.access: Open-source toolkit. Backend extensions and providers have separate setup and access requirements.
tools.limit: A compiled circuit still inherits device noise and resource limits. Backend compatibility needs checking for each program.

tools.name: D-Wave Ocean
tools.summary: Formulate optimization models and sample them with classical, quantum-annealing, or hybrid solvers.
tools.bestFor: Binary quadratic models, Ising formulations, and optimization workflow experiments.
tools.execution: Local classical samplers; D-Wave QPUs and Leap hybrid solvers.
tools.access: Open-source Ocean tools. Leap services require an account and service-specific access.
tools.limit: Classical samplers and hybrid results are not purely quantum computation. Formulation and embedding can dominate performance.

tools.name: QuTiP
tools.summary: Calculate quantum dynamics, including open-system evolution with master-equation and trajectory solvers.
tools.bestFor: Modeling decoherence, driven systems, and small quantum-optics or sensing models.
tools.execution: Classical numerical simulation of quantum systems.
tools.access: Open-source scientific software for local computation.
tools.limit: Results depend on the physical model, basis truncation, and solver assumptions. This is not a hardware job-submission service.

tools.name: Stim
tools.summary: Simulate stabilizer circuits and produce detector samples or error models for error-correction studies.
tools.bestFor: Clifford-circuit experiments, noisy syndrome extraction, and decoder benchmarking workflows.
tools.execution: Fast classical stabilizer simulation; external decoders interpret error syndromes.
tools.access: Open-source library. Local use does not require access to a QPU.
tools.limit: Stim is not a general non-Clifford state-vector simulator and is not itself a decoder.

tools.name: Bloqade
tools.summary: An ecosystem for neutral-atom programming, including analog experiments, circuit simulation, and compilation.
tools.bestFor: Exploring neutral-atom models and QuEra-oriented experimental workflows.
tools.execution: Classical simulation and device-specific experiment submission through supported components.
tools.access: Open-source SDK. Aquila and other device services need the corresponding provider access.
tools.limit: Analog and digital components target different models and devices. Check the relevant component’s documentation before running an experiment.

techniques.name: Gate-based circuits
techniques.summary: Prepare qubits, apply a sequence of gates, and measure selected observables or bit strings.
techniques.bestFor: Expressing digital quantum algorithms and learning how amplitudes become measurement statistics.
steps: Prepare an initial quantum state.
Apply gates and compile for the target’s constraints.
Repeat measurements and interpret sampled results.
techniques.limit: A simulator models an assumed device. Real circuits face connectivity, gate-error, and coherence limits.

techniques.name: Variational quantum eigensolver
techniques.summary: Tune a parameterized quantum state to minimize an estimated Hamiltonian energy using a classical optimizer.
techniques.bestFor: Small chemistry and materials experiments that explore approximate ground-state energies.
steps: Map the physical problem to a qubit Hamiltonian.
Prepare a trial state and estimate its energy.
Update circuit parameters with a classical optimizer.
techniques.limit: Ansatz choice, optimization, noise, and measurement cost constrain accuracy. Practical advantage is problem-dependent and unproven in general.

techniques.name: Quantum approximate optimization
techniques.summary: Alternate cost and mixer operations, then optimize their angles to sample candidate solutions.
techniques.bestFor: Studying combinatorial problems such as Max-Cut and comparing solutions against classical baselines.
steps: Encode an objective in a cost Hamiltonian.
Alternate cost and mixer layers at chosen angles.
Optimize angles, sample candidates, and score them.
techniques.limit: Performance depends on the problem and circuit depth. QAOA does not guarantee efficient solutions to arbitrary hard problems.

techniques.name: Quantum phase estimation
techniques.summary: Use controlled unitary evolution and interference to estimate an eigenphase encoded in a quantum state.
techniques.bestFor: Understanding energy estimation and subroutines behind algorithms such as order finding.
steps: Prepare a state with overlap on a target eigenstate.
Apply controlled powers of a unitary operator.
Interfere the phase register and read an estimate.
techniques.limit: State preparation and precise controlled evolution can be expensive. Large useful instances may require fault-tolerant hardware.

techniques.name: Grover search & amplification
techniques.summary: Amplify marked states through repeated oracle and reflection operations before measurement.
techniques.bestFor: Learning interference-based search and the distinction between query complexity and total runtime.
steps: Prepare a superposition of candidate states.
Mark solutions with an oracle and reflect amplitudes.
Repeat an appropriate number of times and measure.
techniques.limit: The quadratic advantage counts ideal oracle queries. Building the oracle, loading data, and error correction add costs.

techniques.name: Hamiltonian simulation
techniques.summary: Model how a quantum system evolves under its Hamiltonian, using digital circuits, analog controls, or classical solvers.
techniques.bestFor: Exploring interacting spins, materials, molecular dynamics, and controlled quantum models.
steps: Specify a Hamiltonian, initial state, and observables.
Choose a digital, analog, or classical evolution model.
Measure observables and check approximation errors.
techniques.limit: Encoding, approximation, and readout costs matter. A classical solver and a quantum simulator have different scaling and assumptions.

techniques.name: Quantum error correction
techniques.summary: Encode logical information across physical qubits and infer errors from repeated syndrome measurements.
techniques.bestFor: Studying logical qubits, code distances, syndrome extraction, and decoding.
steps: Encode a logical state in a quantum code.
Measure checks to collect error syndromes.
Decode the syndrome and track or apply corrections.
techniques.limit: Error correction needs extra qubits, operations, and decoding. Improvement depends on the code and physical error model.

techniques.name: Error mitigation & suppression
techniques.summary: Reduce noise effects with control strategies or statistical estimators such as zero-noise extrapolation.
techniques.bestFor: Comparing ideal, noisy, and mitigated expectation values in short experimental circuits.
steps: Characterize the circuit, measurements, and noise.
Run a chosen suppression or mitigation strategy.
Compare estimates, uncertainty, and sampling overhead.
techniques.limit: Mitigation can greatly increase sampling cost and retain bias. It does not replace fault-tolerant error correction.

techniques.name: Quantum annealing
techniques.summary: Evolve a system toward a problem Hamiltonian whose low-energy states encode candidate solutions.
techniques.bestFor: Exploring Ising and binary-quadratic formulations and sampling low-energy configurations.
steps: Express an objective and constraints as an energy model.
Map it to the solver and choose an annealing schedule.
Collect samples and assess solution quality.
techniques.limit: Finite temperature, noise, embedding, and schedule affect results. Finding the global optimum or a speedup is not guaranteed.

techniques.name: Variational quantum learning
techniques.summary: Train a parameterized quantum circuit inside a classical learning loop using gradients or other optimizers.
techniques.bestFor: Small hybrid-model experiments and studying quantum feature maps, gradients, and trainability.
steps: Encode data and select a trainable circuit.
Measure outputs and estimate loss gradients.
Update parameters and evaluate against classical baselines.
techniques.limit: Data loading, barren plateaus, noise, and sampling cost can dominate. Better accuracy or speed is not assured.

techniques.name: Quantum interferometry
techniques.summary: Split and recombine coherent paths to turn phase differences into measurable interference patterns.
techniques.bestFor: Understanding optical and atom-based sensing of motion, fields, and gravity.
steps: Prepare coherent light or matter waves.
Let paths acquire different phases through an interaction.
Recombine paths and infer the signal from fringes.
techniques.limit: Coherence, vibration, calibration, and readout limit precision. The double-slit lab illustrates interference, not a complete atom sensor.

techniques.name: Quantum key distribution
techniques.summary: Use quantum states and statistical checks to establish shared key material while testing for disturbance.
techniques.bestFor: Learning basis choice, measurement disturbance, key sifting, and secure-communication assumptions.
steps: Prepare and measure states with chosen bases.
Compare bases and estimate errors over an authenticated channel.
Reconcile errors and apply privacy amplification.
techniques.limit: Security needs authentication, a suitable implementation, and a valid proof. Circuit demonstrations do not constitute a secure QKD system.
